verdict.rationale: Calendly's developer docs describe embedding a scheduling page in your own site or app using inline, popup, or button-trigger styles, each with a snippet of HTML. They also document an Embed API with a `Calendly.initInlineWidget` call. A community report of a shop using a Calendly widget on its homepage independently confirms the embed works in practice. Missing for 10: verbatim popup and floating-widget snippet code (only the inline init call is shown), and explicit 'floating widget' naming beyond 'button trigger'.

support.subject: As a developer, I can embed the booking experience in my own site — inline, popup, or floating widget — with a documented snippet

citations.quote: Embed a scheduling page into your site or app. Choose from inline, popup, or button trigger styles, all with just a snippet of HTML.
To initilize an **inline** embed, use `Calendly.initInlineWidget({url: myLink});`
Embed API: Our simpler, easy-to-use API that lets you add a Calendly landing or booking page to your website.
You can display the scheduling page for users of your app when you initialize one of three embed types based on information from the API such as the scheduling page link.
